Step 1: Assessing your hair quality

  • Do you have lots of breakage? Split ends? Is your hair really dry even after you used plenty of conditioner? Does it tangle more easily? Those are the things you need to consider, the worse any of these "symptoms" are the bigger the chance is of totally ruining your hair.

  • If your hair is dyed already, with any color, you need to realize that there is a big chance parts of your hair wont ever turn blonde. This means cutting your hair, sometimes cutting up to 20/30 cm.

  • If you still feel like bleaching keep in mind that if the bleach goes wrong you might end up having to shave your hair of or cut of most of it.

  • Have you bleached your hair before? If so make sure you go through your hair when its wet, if ANY part of your hair has a bubblegum texture, gooey and stretchy, DO NOT BLEACH!

Step 2: Bleaching

If you have light hair that is not already dyed I recommend not using ultra strength or highlight bleaching it will only cause unnecessary damage. If you have the means bleach at a hairdresser they can adapt the strength of the bleach and asses your hair quality the best.

  • Ok, so you bought your bleach, now read the instructions on the package.

  • Make sure you cover any surfaces that might get stained with old sheets/rags/towels, wear a t-shirt you don't care about and a old towel over your shoulders.

  • It's best if you have a friend that can help you but if you don't you will need two mirrors, so you can see the back of your head while applying bleach. Use plastic gloves.

  • Make sure to check every 10-15 minutes how light your hair has become by taking a strand of hair and scraping some of the bleach of, to prevent damaging your hair more than necessary. Do not exceed the time limit mentioned on the box.

  • Wear a plastic bag over your hair/head to prevent staining and to speed up the bleaching process, heat makes it go faster, you can use a hairdryer to warm up the hair while wearing a plastic bag but don't do it more than 5 or so minutes.

  • When you are satisfied with the color wash the bleach out with lukewarm water, make sure you scrub your scalp to get rid of any residue. Your hair may appear darker,slightly red or yellow while wet. You can use shampoo but its not necessary. If you got a after treatment in the box use it now.

  • If you are going to apply another dye right after bleaching do not use any conditioner or treatment that might have come with the box of bleach.

Step 3: Caring for your hair

  • Always use heath protection when blow drying, using a straightener, curling iron or similar.

  • Use shampoo and/or conditioner that gives alot of moisture, or if you like only wash with conditioner or "no-poo shampoo" (without sulfates), also do not wash your hair more than 3 times a week. You can also use a blue shampoo/silver shampoo to remove yellow tones.

  • Apply a deep conditioner or treatment once a week, I love Olaplex but the most important is moisture!

  • Avoid brushing/combing, styling and teasing your hair to often as it may cause additional breakage.

  • Cut/trim your hair every 6-8 weeks, by yourself or at a hairdresser, be aware that you might not be able to grow out your hair that much.

  • If you need to bleach your roots, bleach ONLY your roots you dont want to damage the already bleached hair further.

  • The sun will damage your hair so wear a hat or a scarf on sunny days. If you are going to a pool use a swim cap, the chlorine in the pool can turn bleached hair green in the worst case.

Step 4: Need to bleach again to get it lighter?

  • Assess your hair quality again, be aware that you might need to cut it off if it goes wrong.

  • Try to space the bleaches out a week or so to give your hair a little breather.

  • Try to limit the time the bleach is in your hair as much as possible to prevent damage.
